ex: The sheikh welcomed the guests to his palace.
A local sheikh paid for the new school.
The sheikh owns many expensive horses and cars.
Reporters waited outside to speak with the sheikh.
The new recruits arrived at the army base today.
Every recruit trains hard for twelve weeks.
He was a young recruit when the war started.
The army needs more recruits this year.
recruit.note: Most often "recruit" is a verb: "We need to recruit new workers."

ex: In the UK, you pay for things in sterling.
Sterling fell against the dollar this week.
Can I change my dollars into sterling here?
The value of sterling rose a little today.
sterling.note: Uncountable. Often "pound sterling": the money of the UK.

ex: In English, "a" and "the" are articles.
Use the article "an" before a vowel sound.
Do I need an article before this word?
You forgot the article in this sentence.
article.note: Most often "article" means a text in a newspaper: "I read an article about Kyiv."

ex: The sultan lived in a huge palace.
The sultan ruled the country for many years.
We visited the tomb of an old sultan.
The sultan welcomed guests from many countries.
The commentator got excited after the goal.
He works as a TV commentator.
The political commentator spoke about the vote.
Sports commentators often talk very fast.
This reef is made of living coral.
Coral grows very slowly in the sea.
We saw bright coral when we went diving.
Please don't touch the coral when you swim.
coral.note: Usually uncountable: "a lot of coral". Also a pink-orange color.

ex: He rides his scooter to work every day.
Can we rent a scooter for the day?
My scooter needs gas before the trip.
A scooter is easy to park in the city.
scooter.note: "Scooter" can also mean a kick scooter or an electric scooter.

jam.note: Uncountable: some jam. "Jam" also often means a traffic jam: too many cars on the road.

ex: I bought a mug as a souvenir.
She brought me a souvenir from Japan.
Where can I buy cheap souvenirs here?
Keep this ticket as a souvenir of the trip.
There is a new tattoo salon near my house.
Is this tattoo salon open on Sundays?
She works as an artist at a tattoo salon.
The tattoo salon uses new needles every time.
tattoo salon.note: More often called a "tattoo shop" or "tattoo parlor".

ex: Press the brake pedal gently at the light.
My foot slipped off the bike pedal.
Push the gas pedal to go faster.
This piano has three pedals at the bottom.
pedal.note: "Gas pedal" in the US; "accelerator" in the UK.

ex: The medic helped the injured soldier.
A medic arrived at the scene in minutes.
She worked as a medic in the army.
Call a medic! Someone is hurt here.
The moral of the story is to be kind.
Every old fairy tale has a moral.
What is the moral of this story?
The moral is simple: do not lie to friends.
moral.note: Most often "moral" is an adjective: "a moral choice". Good rules of life are "morals".

ex: Is there an English equivalent of this word?
Ten dollars is the equivalent of nine euros.
What is the Ukrainian equivalent of this phrase?
This car costs the equivalent of a year's pay.
equivalent.note: Often an adjective: "One mile is equivalent to 1.6 kilometers."

ex: Capitalism is based on private business and profit.
We talked about capitalism in history class.
Some people think capitalism is unfair to workers.
He wrote a book about capitalism and money.
The drummer counted to four and started the song.
He is the drummer in a rock band.
Our drummer was late to practice again.
Do you know a good drummer for our band?

copyright.note: Do not mix it up with "copywriting" (writing texts for ads).

ex: He had an alibi for the night of the crime.
The police checked her alibi carefully.
His friend gave him a false alibi.
Do you have an alibi for last night?
Pardon? I didn't hear you, sorry.
Pardon me, is this seat free?
Pardon me, could you say that again?
Pardon me, I did not see you there.
pardon.note: Often "pardon" means official forgiveness for a crime: "The president gave him a pardon."

ex: I finally finished the last level of the game.
This level of the game is really hard.
You need more points to reach the next level.
How do I get past this level?
level.note: Most often "level" means how high or good something is: "a high level of English."

ex: I'd like a hamburger and fries, please.
He grilled hamburgers in the backyard.
This hamburger is too big to eat.
Kids usually love hamburgers with cheese.
hamburger.note: In everyday speech, people often say "burger".

ex: The Roman legion marched into the city.
He joined the French Foreign Legion at twenty.
A Roman legion had thousands of soldiers.
The legion fought bravely in the battle.
legion.note: Also "legions of" = very many: "legions of fans".

ex.note: Informal: a former partner (ex-boyfriend, ex-girlfriend, ex-wife).

reception.note: Also a formal party: "a wedding reception". In US hotels, often "the front desk".

ex: The number pi is about 3.14.
Use pi to find the area of a circle.
She learned pi to fifty digits for fun.
Multiply the diameter of the circle by pi.
A bot answered my question on the website.
Many social media accounts are actually bots.
This bot sends me the weather every morning.
He built a simple bot for his online shop.

safe.note: Most often "safe" is an adjective, "not dangerous": "Is it safe here?"

renaissance.note: Capitalized for the historical period: "the Renaissance".

ex: Our office uses a proxy server for the internet.
Can I connect through a proxy server at work?
The proxy server blocks some websites at school.
Turn off the proxy server if the page does not load.
Our website gets a lot of traffic.
Web traffic grew after the new ad.
How much traffic does your blog get?
We check the traffic to our page every week.
traffic.note: Most often "traffic" means cars on the road: "There is a lot of traffic today."

ex: My grandfather is in the hospital with pneumonia.
She caught pneumonia last winter and stayed home.
Pneumonia can be very dangerous for babies.
The doctor said it was pneumonia.
The hotel hosted a big wedding banquet.
We went to the school awards banquet last night.
The banquet had five courses and a cake.
The guests danced after the banquet ended.
The case went to a special tribunal.
The tribunal made its decision on Friday.
An international tribunal judged the war crimes.
He appeared before the tribunal last month.
